motions.topic: GENERALIZATION TEST (Option B): determine whether the paratope-density ranking identifies a GENERAL motif or a TEMPLATE-specific artifact, purely structurally, no structure prediction. Measure: (a) density (contacts/residue) vs antigen atom count across the 7,786 scored complexes -- if density is independent of antigen size it is an antibody property (a motif), if it rises with antigen size it is partly an antigen artifact; (b) cross-antigen transfer -- take the top-density paratope and score it against a DIFFERENT corpus antigen (coordinate-translated to the same frame) and report whether the density holds. REJECT AS PREMATURE: any design step that scores a seeded sequence with the same contacts/residue metric (a fixed point, not a loop); claiming generalization without the cross-antigen measurement. MEASURED: 7,786 antibody-antigen complexes scored (contacts/residue density, mean 84.2 contacts, 12.24 residues). The scorer counts contacts between ATOMS in resolved crystal structures. A designed antibody is a SEQUENCE; scoring it needs structure prediction (AlphaFold/ESMFold + complex docking), none of which is in-tree. The density ranking is ordered by contacts-per-residue; scoring a template-seeded design with the SAME metric is high by construction. The + placeholder finding means single-domain (VHH) and paired-chain antibodies are distinct classes.

CONTACT-MODEL RUNG (Option A): build a sequence-to-density predictor trained on the 7,786 verified complexes (sequence -> paratope contact count), held-out test. This is the honest rung between 'count contacts in crystals' and 'score designed sequences' -- it uses existing data and produces a measurably testable evaluator. REJECT AS PREMATURE: claiming sequence-level scoring without a held-out tolerance; conflating VHH (single-chain) with paired-chain antibodies in the training set (keep the classes separate).
